before_text: We propose a weakly supervised semantic segmentation method that utilizes large quantities and diversities in unlabeled videos to produce accurate, high-resolution results quickly. Our method utilizes motion cues found in video sequences to localize objects and classes. These cues are learned by an offline classifier, and their predictions are used as initial seed sets to propagate via graph cut optimization. Our method utilizes both spatial and temporal structural information, giving our system a good performance over static image-only learning frameworks as reported in literature. We also incorporate recent work, such as Deep Features (a Convolutional Neural Network), to improve overall accuracy and efficiency without significantly increasing run time cost. Our method significantly outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods such as PropNet and LTFS2K+N on public benchmark datasets such as Cityscapes, MPII, and CamVid, which are densely and significantly varied in their labeled regions.

before_text: This paper introduces a novel method for addressing a single erbium ion within a silicon crystal using a focused laser beam. Erbium ions are introduced into the silicon lattice through implantation. And their optical properties make them ideal for quantum information processing and other photonic applications.  Current techniques for addressing individual erbium ions in silicon involve electrical methods, which are limited by the difficulty in precisely controlling the ion's position and electric field strength. Our proposed optical approach offers several advantages, including high spatial resolution, low power consumption, and the ability to address multiple ions simultaneously.  In our experiments, a focused laser beam with a radius of approximately 1 micrometer was used to address a single erbium ion in silicon. By tuning the laser frequency to the ion's resonant transition, a clear signature of ion-photon interaction was observed, indicating the successful addressing of the individual ion.  Our results open the door to the development of scalable, densely-packed arrays of individually-addressable erbium ions in silicon; Which could enable a new generation of quantum information processing and photonic devices. By utilizing the unique properties of rare-earth ions in silicon, this work contributes to the advancement of quantum computing and other photonic applications.

before_text: The European Parliament has ordered a revision of its ambitious plans to create a unified patent system across Europe.  The assembly's legal affairs committee stated that the package, known as the unitary patent, would be rewritten to address critics' concerns.  These included the involvement of the European Court of Justice, the need for translation, and the validity of patents in all EU states.  The legislation aims to simplify patent protection by allowing inventors to gain patent protection in a single, unified patent court.  The legislation faces resistance from Italy, Spain, and Poland, who have threatened to block the plan unless changes are made.  The committee plans to split the unitary patent package into two bills.  One will deal with the unitary patent itself, while the other will establish a new court to handle patent disputes, known as the Unified Patent Court (UPC).  Italian socialist Guido Sacconi, who led the work on the report, said the committee had decided to "take the bull by the horns."  "We have decided to modify the two pillars of the unitary patent package: the unitary patent itself and the Unified Patent Court," he explained.  "Both elements will be divided. Which allows us to proceed first with the patent court and later discuss the unitary patent."  The revised proposal will now go before the full parliament for a vote.  If passed, it will then be up to the 28 member states to decide whether to implement the plan.
